title: Kochhar Wipes Out Loans for 176 NC State Grads
excerpt: Indian-American philanthropist Anil Kochhar honours his father's Punjab-to-Raleigh journey with a stunning commencement gift
body:
Indian-American philanthropist Anil Kochhar stopped a graduation ceremony cold on May 8 when he announced, mid-speech, that he and his wife Marilyn would pay off every final-year education loan held by graduates of NC State's Wilson College of Textiles for the 2025-26 academic year.

**What happened at Reynolds Coliseum:**
Kochhar made the surprise announcement at the college's 2026 commencement, where roughly 176 graduates — many earning degrees in textile engineering, fashion design, and polymer and colour chemistry — learned their recent student debt would be erased through the Kochhars' gift. The announcement was met with thunderous applause and a standing ovation as students realised the financial burden of their final-year loans had been lifted.

**Why this gift carries an 80-year backstory:**
Prakash Chand Kochhar became only the second Indian student to enrol at the Wilson College of Textiles in 1946, completing a bachelor's degree in textile manufacturing in 1950 and a master's two years later before building a career in textile engineering. In 1986, a year after Prakash Chand Kochhar's death, his wife Christine Hayes Kochhar started the Prakash Chand Kochhar Memorial Textile Scholarship at the university where they first met. Over the years, Anil and Marilyn expanded those efforts through multiple endowments supporting faculty recruitment, graduate research and student opportunities.

**Why this resonates beyond one campus:**
The announcement reignited debate around the growing student debt crisis in the United States, where borrowers collectively owe more than $1.7 trillion in education loans, according to US government data cited in media reports. Wilson College Dean David Hinks said: 'I could not be more grateful to Anil and Marilyn for this extraordinary investment in our newest Wilson for Life alumni. One of our primary goals is to make the Wilson College affordable for all, and Anil and Marilyn are helping us achieve it.'

**What to watch next:**
Watch whether the Kochhar family's three newly established endowments — covering the dean's chair, faculty recruitment, and graduate research — signal a longer-term institutional partnership that deepens the family's multi-generational ties to NC State.
